title: Trump Threatens 50% Tariffs on Canadian Autos, Auto Parts, and Steel Starting Jan. 1, 2027
detail: Two days after Canada-US trade talks collapsed and Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Sept. 8 retaliatory tariffs, President Trump escalated further on Monday, threatening to raise tariffs on Canadian automobiles, auto parts, and steel to 50% effective January 1, 2027. Trump posted that companies should 'Build in the U.S. and there are ZERO TARIFFS,' and called Canada 'among the worst Nations in the World to deal with.' General Motors and Ford shares fell roughly 1-3% on the threat, and the announcement further clouded the outlook for the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement's scheduled 2026 joint review.

title: Tech Selloff Deepens on Apple-CXMT Chip Rumor and Alibaba's $10.2B Share Sale
detail: US stocks opened the week sharply diverging: the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose about 0.2% to 53,374.96, the lone major index in the green, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.35% to 7,647.82 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.71% to 25,995.05 as investors rotated out of high-flying AI-linked tech names into defensive and value sectors. Semiconductor stocks led the declines on reports that Apple is testing chips from China's CXMT as an alternative supplier, while Alibaba's announcement of a $10.2 billion share sale to fund AI infrastructure investment added further pressure on the sector. Gold rose about 1% toward three-month highs on 'debasement trade' concerns tied to US debt levels, and bitcoin surged over 3%. The moves came at the start of a closely watched week featuring Nvidia's Wednesday earnings report and the Fed's Jackson Hole symposium later in the week.
